meeting_header:
Date: 2027-12-15 | Time: 16:00 PST | Duration: 45m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Evan Ruiz (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood CSM), Alicia Gray (Harbor Head Eng), Dr. Kevin Park (Harbor CTO), Liam O'Neil (Harbor DevOps), Sofia Martinez (Harbor Security), Jamal Rivers (Product)
summary: Kickoff for Harbor Health's Redwood onboarding. Covered high-level deployment options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), security/compliance needs (SOC2, KMS, audit logs), network requirements for VPC/on-prem, initial success criteria and timeline. Agreed action items and next steps to move toward a pilot and perf bench.
topics: Deployment options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
Security & compliance: SOC2, KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML
Initial PoC success criteria and timeline
Operational concerns: routing, KV cache, batching, cost
transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep this to about 45 minutes. Quick intros?
[00:00:18] Alicia Gray: Hi Alicia from Harbor, head of eng, excited to get started.
[00:00:25] Dr. Kevin Park: Kevin here, CTO, focus on compliance + infra.
[00:00:30] Liam O'Neil: Liam, DevOps, I'll own the network side.
[00:00:34] Maya Chen: Awesome, from Redwood we have Evan SE and Samir CSM, we'll run through onboarding flow, security, and next steps.
[00:00:50] Evan Ruiz: Quick note, we'll cover Hosted API for fast start, Dedicated for reserved capacity, and Private (VPC/on-prem) for regulated workloads.
[00:01:22] Jamal Rivers: Our main drivers are latency and PHI handling — data residency is a must. We want to avoid vendor lock but need audit logs and KMS integration.
[00:01:40] Samir Patel: Got it, our onboarding checklist includes SOC2 docs, KMS patterns, and an audit log example. I'll share the doc after this call.
[00:02:05] Sofia Martinez: On encryption, we need to know if Redwood can integrate with our AWS KMS/HSM and if keys can be customer-managed. Also SSO and SCIM for RBAC.
[00:02:38] Evan Ruiz: Yes, Private supports customer-managed KMS, and we have SAML/SSO + SCIM for user provisioning. For Dedicated we can do VPC peering and bring-your-own-keys.
[00:03:10] Alicia Gray: Timelines — we'd like pilot by end of January, production by end of Q1. Is that realistic?
[00:03:22] Maya Chen: That's feasible. Typical pattern: 2-3 week onboarding for Hosted; Dedicated/Private takes longer — 4-8 weeks depending on networking and approvals.
[00:03:47] Liam O'Neil: For VPC peering we need a clear network diagram. We'll need IPs, routing and maybe a transit gateway.
[00:03:59] Evan Ruiz: We'll send an infra checklist with EIP ranges and firewall rules. Note: for on-prem we support air-gapped packages but that'll add time.
[00:04:25] Dr. Kevin Park: SLA question: for Dedicated what's the uptime SLA and latency targets?
[00:04:31] Maya Chen: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and configured latency SLOs; we'll share the SLA doc. Typical p95 latency depends on model/sequence length but we provide profiles.
[00:04:58] Jamal Rivers: Cost concerns — we care about per-token cost but also predictable capacity.
[00:05:05] Evan Ruiz: We can size Dedicated pools and show cost tradeoffs; Optimize tooling suggests batching/quantization settings to lower unit cost.
[00:05:31] Alicia Gray: For the pilot we plan to route sensitive traffic to Private and non-sensitive to Hosted. Is routing policy supported?
[00:05:41] Evan Ruiz: Yes, smart routing by policy is supported — you can route by latency, cost, region, or a toggle at the app layer.
[00:06:05] Samir Patel: We'll include a sample routing policy in the repo we share.
[00:06:22] Liam O'Neil: Any special network requirements for KV cache or continuous batching? We run a heavy token-per-request workload and want to avoid cold cache penalties.
[00:06:33] Evan Ruiz: KV cache is managed by the runtime; we'll advise on warmup patterns. Note — sometimes transcriptions say K V cash, but it's KV cache (key-value). We'll include guidance to keep prefix caches warm and TTLs.
[00:07:05] Sofia Martinez: Audit logs — need retention for 2 years and immutable logs for compliance. Does Redwood support extended log retention?
[00:07:16] Maya Chen: Yes, extended observability retention is an add-on. We can push logs to your S3 or a SIEM and enable immutable logging for audit.
[00:07:47] Dr. Kevin Park: Pen test / attestation — do you provide pen test reports and can we conduct a joint security assessment?
[00:07:55] Evan Ruiz: We have internal reports and can enter an NDA for detailed artifacts; we also support customer-led assessments for Private deployments.
[00:08:20] Jamal Rivers: Ok cool. On success criteria for pilot — what should we agree on? Latency targets, throughput, accuracy metrics?
[00:08:30] Maya Chen: Proposed pilot success criteria: 1) Achieve p95 latency under X ms for our median prompt length, 2) Throughput target of 1k rps for peak tests, 3) Quality regression <= 2% on eval set, 4) Integration with customer KMS and SSO.
[00:08:56] Alicia Gray: For X ms, can you give a ballpark?
[00:09:01] Evan Ruiz: Ballpark depends on model variant — for a medium open model p95 with proper batching could be ~150-300ms on Dedicated, hosted may be slightly higher. We'll put numbers in the sizing doc.
[00:09:26] Liam O'Neil: We want to run a perf benchmark with a 1k rps profile, can Redwood run that or do we need to simulate?
[00:09:33] Evan Ruiz: We can coordinate to run the benchmark together — SE-led. We'll need sample prompts and traffic pattern.
[00:09:57] Samir Patel: I'll make a checklist: share prompts, define latency/throughput targets, schedule a bench run with Evan.
[00:10:10] Jamal Rivers: Any red flags on storage of PHI?
[00:10:18] Maya Chen: For PHI we recommend Private + customer-managed KMS and enforce retention policies. We also support data isolation in Dedicated.
[00:10:40] Dr. Kevin Park: What about model updates and rollouts? We need canary deploys and automatic fallbacks.
[00:10:47] Evan Ruiz: Redwood Console supports canary deploys, A/B tests, and automatic fallback policies if a rollout causes regressions. We'll show the console flow in next demo.
[00:11:25] Alicia Gray: Integrations — do you have a list of SDKs and language support?
[00:11:32] Maya Chen: Yes, JS, Python, and REST. We also have examples for embedding/reranking and a Git repo with quickstarts.
[00:11:50] Liam O'Neil: For network security, do you require outbound-only peering or inbound?
[00:11:57] Evan Ruiz: Mostly outbound with VPC peering; for VPC peering we provide endpoints and IP ranges. We'll send specifics.
[00:12:20] Jamal Rivers: Ok, let's talk timeline and owners.
[00:12:27] Maya Chen: Proposed timeline: Dec 17 - onboarding deck and SOC2 + infra checklist. Dec 20 - Harbor shares network diagram. Week of Jan 3 - private deployment planning call. Jan 8-12 - bench run. Jan 26 - pilot review.
[00:12:45] Alicia Gray: That aligns with internal approvals.
[00:12:55] Sophia Martinez: (typo) - Sofia. I'll compile compliance questions by 12/18.
[00:13:05] Evan Ruiz: We'll prepare Dedicated sizing and a cost estimate; note quantization and batching can reduce cost by 20-40% depending on model.
[00:13:33] Maya Chen: Action recap — Samir will send the onboarding doc and SOC2 links, Evan will send sizing + bench plan, Maya will share pricing and SLA, Harbor will send network diagram and compliance list.
[00:13:58] Dr. Kevin Park: Sounds good. Can we get a calendar invite for the infra deep dive?
[00:14:04] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll calendar that for the week of Jan 3.
[00:14:20] Jamal Rivers: A few small notes — we evaluated Anthropic and some on-prem stacks, our main tie-breakers are security posture and predictable cost.
[00:14:34] Evan Ruiz: Understood. We'll include comparative notes and references to our performance profiles.
[00:14:50] Alicia Gray: Any docs you recommend we review before the next call?
[00:14:56] Samir Patel: We'll share the onboarding checklist, the SLA, SOC2 summary, and a sample network diagram. Links will be in the follow-up email.
[00:15:18] Jamal Rivers: Great, thanks everyone.
[00:15:22] Maya Chen: Thanks all — we'll send next steps and action items now.
[00:15:30] [end of recording]

Notes: transcription has occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "K V cash" for KV cache). Shared artifacts referenced: onboarding deck (link sent after call), SOC2 summary (link), infra checklist (link).
